decision: Tightened Ep 1 script to 12 lines / 76 words (~27 s cartoon, ~36 s total)
why: Series format targets 30-40 s; cartoon 25-32 s; lessons rule: real footage 4-5 s then the teaser card

decision: No phone hand-off in Ep 1; Gus's 'Depends on the spray' is the button and cuts straight to real spray footage
why: Keeps it short and sets up Ep 9 without making a removal claim before the owner confirms the spray type

decision: Dropped the FULL VIDEO teaser card; Ep 1 ends on the logo card
why: Owner note 2026-11-16 (lessons.md): teaser card only when a matching full video exists; none exists for spraying, and the open question hands off to Ep 9

decision: End on the logo card alone, no CTA line
why: Owner note 2026-11-16 (lessons.md): CTA only when relevant; Ep 1 explains scanning, not a scan for sale

decision: Script v2: spray only glass/chrome/black/badges; 'pattern of light' (no colour); optional tracking-pattern lines; audience question card 'WHAT DO YOU SPRAY WITH?' then logo
why: Owner answers 2026-11-16; Artec spec sheets list a VCSEL 3D light source, so 'white light' would be inaccurate on screen

decision: Proposed Civic EK footage (hatch-glass spray + approved 1:1 match A) instead of the IS350
why: Owner asked for a non-IS350 car; Civic has a glass-spray close-up, a full scan and an already-solved 1:1 cut, so no new solve

decision: Checked script v2 against the new proportions (option 3: shorter torso, bigger head/feet, hands closer); no gag needs changing
why: Gags use eyes (squint), floating-hand pokes and the spray/pattern props, none depend on tall thin bodies or far-out hands

decision: Voice take 1: ElevenLabs v4 dialogue job cd66de56-ff8e-4c87-b849-4e16d0d4558c (Kiki = Pip, Harrison = Gus, emotion tags, all 15 lines incl. the card line), 41.14 s, 3.22 credits; not sped up
why: Owner approved script v2; voices must be approved before animating

decision: Take 1 transcribes word-for-word (faster-whisper small/medium); 0.3 s breath before line 10b is partly voiced, owner to confirm it reads as a sigh, not the word
why: Emotion tags can be read aloud; check by ear

decision: Timing: speech 32.4 s; cartoon ~37 s with 0.3-0.4 s gaps between lines (no tightening inside lines), so the episode lands ~45 s, over the 30-40 s target. Dropping 10a/10b would bring it to ~39 s
why: Flagged to the owner rather than speeding up the voices (standing rule)

decision: 10a/10b picture: squiggles sprayed on the door plus tape strips on the roof; voice unchanged ('Why the squiggles?')
why: Owner: squiggles, but sometimes tape; the approved take stays, so the tape is shown, not spoken

decision: Real footage: SL600 clip (owner_1) caption-free 23.8-32 s for the beats - headlight glass 24.4, tracking stripes on black door 27.0, chrome star badge 29.0 - then Civic windshield pull-back -> 1:1 cut on cam_A -> Civic scan
why: Owner clips show exactly the episode's points on a black car; the rest of owner_1 and all of owner_3 carry burned-in captions/prices (no text over IRL); the Civic 1:1 is already solved and approved, an SL600 1:1 would need a new solve on a 720p clip

decision: Cartoon built on the pilot's locked scene (partA_scene.py --exec ep1_scene.py): ray-cast stripe pattern, see-through glass, chrome reflection, fading black, sprayed coat, squiggles + roof tape, '?' and tracking rings
why: Reuses the series' locked characters/look exactly; the pattern is real geometry so it bends over creases and the glass/chrome/black failures are physically readable

decision: Cartoon rendered on twos (EEVEE, 1080x1920, 8 spp, every 2nd frame held), ~30 s/frame -> ~4.7 h
why: On ones would be ~9.4 h; holding frames is standard cartoon timing and the camera pushes are small

decision: Civic scan rebuilt exactly as the Civic reel (3 mm decimate, crop, yaw -14.725, prep --drop-islands 3000); onion at cam_A f150 shows no ghosting
why: cam_A was solved against that transform; reproducing the chain keeps the approved 1:1 match without a new solve

decision: Series v0.4: episode renumbered to Ep 2 in script.md; callback/ending changes recorded as pending owner, render not stopped
why: Relayed series note conflicts with the owner's direct ending instruction and the approved take; the opening shot is the only cartoon shot it would replace

decision: Music: pilot bed inquisitive_A (Higgsfield 077bbd23, identified by its bass-free intro and bass entry 19.245 s); intro extended 8 bars with the pilot's 2-bar back-jumps (30->22 played twice); lift lands on the real cut (measured 39.224 vs 39.200 s); pilot v3 route 40->56 to the real ending; final chord under the logo (48.83 vs 48.80 s)
why: Owner: reuse the pilot's track; same structure the owner approved in the pilot

decision: Real-footage cuts on beats (18/18/18/36/54 frames = 0.6 s beats), card 90 f, logo 90 f; total 1500 f = 50.0 s
why: Pilot music route fixes card/logo lengths; real section stays 4.8 s

decision: after_cartoon.sh waits on the Blender process (partA_scene.py) instead of render_ep1.sh
why: pgrep -f render_ep1.sh matched the parent 'bash -c ... render_ep1.sh ...; after_cartoon.sh' chain line, so the scan step waited forever after the cartoon finished

decision: Caption pages end at their shot's cut; picture cache keyed to the gfx render
why: Pip's 'Does it come off?' ran 4 frames into Gus's close-up across his eyes; and video.mp4 was reused after a caption change, so the CAP_Y fix silently didn't reach the output

decision: Fender badge moved from (1.48, 0.72) to (1.80, 0.64): on the front fender ahead of the wheel arch; re-rendered only the 201 frames where either position is in frame (F, G, I, K)
why: owner: the badge was rendered on a tire. The old spot was inside the arch circle (r 0.45). A camera-frustum probe (EP1_PROBE) found the affected frames, so the fix costs ~1.6 h instead of a full 4.7 h re-render

decision: Alt ending ep2_v2_black: at the logo cut (frame 1410, on the beat) the question card pans off left over 18 frames (ease-in) into the card's own black; holds black to 50.0 s; audio identical to v2
why: owner wants a no-logo alternative alongside the final v2; panning the card (not a dissolve) keeps the cut on the beat, and filling with the card tone avoids a visible seam between #0b0c0b and pure black
